subject.title: [Bug] sessions_yield on a required-completion spawned run finalizes the task as blocked ("Required completion did not produce a final deliverable") at first turn end; the real final reply never announces

question: Should this be fixed as a narrow required-completion `sessions_yield` lifecycle hardening bug, or folded into the broader yielded-subagent delivery work already in flight?
rationale: Current main has an intended explicit-yield pause path, but the reported live runs and source fallback show a credible marker-loss or ordering gap; choosing the durable fix boundary needs maintainer ownership before automation branches.

options.title: Narrow lifecycle hardening
options.body: Add a focused guard and regression/live proof for first-turn `sessions_yield` required-completion runs so they cannot finalize as blocked before resumed final output.

options.title: Fold into delivery cluster
options.body: Track this under the broader yielded-subagent delivery and announce retry work, landing one coordinated fix for the overlapping wake and delivery states.

options.title: Live repro first
options.body: Require a packaged gateway reproduction on current main before selecting the code boundary, accepting slower resolution for stronger proof.

recommendation.title: Narrow lifecycle hardening
recommendation.body: Add a focused guard and regression/live proof for first-turn `sessions_yield` required-completion runs so they cannot finalize as blocked before resumed final output.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on how the required-completion blocked contract should interact with yielded subagent lifecycle state.
